npcRoster.name: Vellum Tekt
npcRoster.publicDescription:
Vellum Tekt is a fast-talking Satyr salesman with old-world polish, nervous charm, and the hollow-eyed exhaustion of someone who spent decades selling safety he was never allowed to receive himself. As a Thalunesh-touched Satyr, he masks trauma with jokes, brochures, rehearsed optimism, and theatrical friendliness, but every locked door and denied refuge still lives under his smile.
At the Eldryssar Clinic, Vellum now works with the Regent Lattice selling bunker berths, reinforced shelter contracts, evacuation ledgers, and “future-proof” survival packages to families afraid of divine breaches, ichor contamination, and civic collapse. He is irritating, pitiable, surprisingly useful, and desperate to matter again—especially if someone gives him a real settlement post instead of treating him like a relic from a failed sales pitch.

Local records favor Altruistic, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Halfling — Stout Halfling, Kender, Kithkin. Satyr reads through the Satyr entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Satyrs are goat-legged fey known for revelry, music, and indulgence in natural pleasures. They often serve as companions of wilderness spirits and chaotic celebration. npcRoster.name: Kasumi Nakren
npcRoster.publicDescription: Kasumi Nakren is a Kender runaway tinkerer whose curiosity is tangled with fear that her memories, body, or family story may not be entirely her own. She fled to Lunethryl chasing answers about identity, constructed life, and hidden communities, but her bravery is still the bravery of someone young enough to mistake danger for proof. The Choral Synod sees her as a vulnerable witness and a brilliant little engineer; she sees herself as a question no adult has answered honestly.
npcRoster.settlementAncestryTexture: Lunethryl is a City in Vaelmyrith, under Council Republic, with severe danger, Beach and reefs with water, Ocean Surface floating settlement, Beach and grass with water terrain, and public routes by Caravan, Train, Steamship, Submarine. Local records favor Neutral, Lawful, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Sea Elf, Tortle, Genasi — Water Genasi. Kender reads through the Kender entry of the race compendium, within Halfling and Smallfolk, marked by Ishtanora. Kender are endlessly curious wanderers with a fearless approach to danger and novelty. They often collect objects impulsively, driven by an almost compulsive sense of exploration. Table cues: Fearless, Kender Aptitude, Taunt; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Cooperative - Pragmatic.
publicRumors: Kasumi Nakren knows why an ichor ledger changed hands last Enkirday.
Kasumi Nakren has a contact in Zarveng who will deny everything.

npcRoster.name: Stockton Oldroad
npcRoster.publicDescription: Stockton Oldroad is a kindly but stubborn Jaspey caravan patron who hides dangerous compassion behind slow speech, old blankets, and boring invoices. He uses The Brass Concordat routes to move food, medicine, and people with changed names, especially those fleeing the Glasswell Institute or ichor-debt bondage. Stockton looks harmless until someone threatens a traveler under his protection; then every wagon, innkeeper, and toll clerk he has ever helped becomes part of the escape plan.

npcRoster.name: Nira Prizewheel
npcRoster.publicDescription: Nira Prizewheel is a gender-less Lorwyn Changeling mascot guide whose cheerful voice, bright gestures, and scripted tourist patter barely conceal a savage understanding of how dangerous the carnival really is. At the Sylthera-Vael Guild Desk, they give directions, sell the dream, warn clever visitors in coded jokes, and remember every broken attraction the Nefaric Veil forgot to make safe. Nira is funny, useful, and privately furious at being treated like decoration when they may be the only guide still trying to keep guests alive.
npcRoster.settlementAncestryTexture: Sylthéra-Vael is a Village in Vaelmyrith, under Council Republic, with low danger, Marshes and swamps, Partial forest, Beach and grass with water terrain, and public routes by Caravan, Train, Ferry, Steamship. Local records favor Altruistic, Neutral, Cooperative, Honorable civic habits; common communities include Human, Halfling — Lightfoot Halfling, Elf — Wood Elf, Elf — Eladrin, Fey-Folk — Faerie. Lorwyn Changeling reads through the Lorwyn Changeling entry of the race compendium, within Fey and Trickster Folk, marked by Thalunesh. Lorwyn changelings are fey-adapted shapeshifters tied to idyllic, magical realms. They often blend seamlessly into multiple cultures and identities. Table cues: Shape Self, Darkvision, Delightful Imitator, Unpredictable Movement; starting tendency Altruistic - Chaotic - Neutral - Pragmatic.

areaModel.method: Earth-sized spherical Voronoi province territory model
areaModel.reason: The province JSON files contain locked province center latitude/longitude coordinates, but no hand-drawn province border polygons. areaModel.precisionNote: Areas are model-exact for the spherical Voronoi territory model and rounded to 6 decimal places in output.

globalNamedWeatherDefinitions.What it means: When both moons favor the sea at once, harbor stones vanish and reef roads drown.
A low, quiet tide that exposes mud gates, wreck bones, and hidden causeways.
A low-pressure sea storm arriving with a strong moon tide.
A sudden retreat of water before trench-fed surge returns.
A black-green wall of rain that crosses whole coasts.
Short, sharp squalls that arrive in pairs or trios every few days.
Moonlit fog so bright it makes ships look closer than they are.
A towering thunderhead that forms over heated highlands.
Greenish swamp fog carrying spores, firefly light, and bad directions.
A suffocating, windless heat that freezes sails and tempers alike.
A rotating storm whose calm center is ringed by clear, staring sky.
Low rolling thunder that repeats long before the rain reaches a settlement.
Warm gas-fog from marsh canals and low cave mouths.
A fine crosswind rain that seems to fall sideways from many directions.
Shimmering heat that turns distance into false water and false stone.
Three winds meeting over cliffs, reefs, or a canyon mouth.
A steep, dark swell pushed by far-off pressure changes.
Warm rain that wakes rot, swollen roots, and hungry fungus.
A sudden evening wind that turns forest travel loud and blind.
A hooked dust plume ahead of dryline storms.
Highland lightning that walks along exposed ridges.
Rain-soaked clay roads that swallow carts and boots.
A season when road puddles hide sinkholes, leeches, and false bottoms.
A dry graveyard wind that carries dust, spores, and old sickness.
A clean mountain lift used by skyships and great birds.
A fast pull beneath reef water during strong tide shifts.
Thin cold rain that whistles through ruins and empty rigging.
One storm-fed river splits into several dangerous surges.
A spiraling river or sea current that turns boats sideways.
A soft glowing insect and spore bloom after warm moon rain.
